pivotal_trials.trial_name: AURA Extension (Study D5160C00001, Phase 2 component; labeled Study 1)
pivotal_trials.phase: Phase 2 (dose-expansion component of first-in-human AURA trial)
pivotal_trials.design: Open-label, non-randomized, non-comparative, multiple cohort single-arm trial; all patients received osimertinib 80 mg once daily
pivotal_trials.population: Metastatic EGFR T790M mutation-positive NSCLC (by cobas EGFR mutation test) progressing on prior EGFR TKI therapy
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Confirmed overall response rate (ORR), durable for at least 4 weeks, by blinded independent review committee

nct_ctgov.title: AZD9291 First Time In Patients Ascending Dose Study

pivotal_trials.design: Open-label, non-randomized, non-comparative, multiple parallel cohort single-arm study of osimertinib 80 mg once daily
pivotal_trials.population: Metastatic EGFR T790M mutation-positive NSCLC (by cobas EGFR mutation test) progressing after a prior EGFR TKI
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Confirmed overall response rate (ORR), durable for at least 4 weeks, by blinded independent review committee
pivotal_trials.result: Confirmed ORR 61% (95% CI 54, 68) by BICR; pooled across both studies (N=411) ORR 59% (95% CI 54, 64)

nct_ctgov.title: Phase II AZD9291 Open Label Study in NSCLC After Previous EGFR TKI Therapy in EGFR and T790M Mutation Positive Tumours

key_safety: Most common (>20%) adverse reactions: diarrhea (42%), rash (41%), dry skin (31%), nail toxicity (25%). Most serious adverse reactions were interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis, cardiomyopathy, and QTc prolongation; fatal ILD occurred in ~0.5% of patients
target_moa: Osimertinib is a kinase inhibitor of EGFR that binds irreversibly to certain mutant forms of EGFR (T790M, L858R, and exon 19 deletion) at ~9-fold lower concentrations than wild-type; it also inhibits HER2, HER3, HER4, ACK1, and BLK

rems.type: REMS not required; risks of ILD/pneumonitis and QTc prolongation can be mitigated through product labeling

companion_dx_detail: cobas EGFR Mutation Test (Roche Molecular Systems) as companion diagnostic to detect EGFR T790M mutation

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee vote occurred because the application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee; FDA stated the safety profile is acceptable and there were no controversial issues that would benefit from advisory committee discussion

description.text: Converted accelerated approval to regular approval for metastatic EGFR T790M mutation-positive NSCLC after progression on EGFR TKI therapy

citations.quote: This Prior Approval sNDA seeks regular approval of osimertinib for the treatment of patients with metastatic epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) T790M mutation-positive non-small cell lung cancer, as detected by an FDA-approved test, whose disease has progressed on or after EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor therapy based on the results of Study D5160C00003 (AURA 3), in fulfillment of PMR 2978-1. This sNDA also proposes to remove the following statement from the currently approved indication: "This indication is approved under accelerated approval based on tumor response rate and duration of response [see Clinical Studies (14)]. Continued approval for this indication may be contingent upon verification and description of clinical benefit in confirmatory trials."

basis.text: Granted priority review (reviewer recommendation: Priority Review) because osimertinib treats a serious, life-threatening condition (metastatic NSCLC) and provides a significant improvement in effectiveness over available therapy

citations.quote: ## **Recommendation:** Priority Review

Metastatic NSCLC is a serious and life-threatening disease with a predicted 5-year survival of 4.2%. Even in the subset of NSCLC with an EGFR mutation-positive NSCLC, the median survival ranges from 19-28 months.

summary.text: Osimertinib received fast track (Nov 6, 2013), orphan drug (Sep 4, 2014), and breakthrough therapy (Apr 16, 2014) designations, and was granted priority review. It was granted accelerated approval based on tumor response rate and duration of response, with a required randomized confirmatory trial to verify clinical benefit.

citations.quote: On November 6, 2013, FDA designated as a Fast Track development program the investigation of AZD9291 for the treatment of patients with metastatic NSCLC (b) (4) and have progressed following prior EGFR TKI therapy, based on the development program designed to demonstrate a clinically important increase in progression-free survival as compared to available therapy.

On September 4, 2014, FDA designated osimertinib (N-(2-{2-dimethylaminoethyl-methylamino}-4-methoxy-5-{[4-(1-methylindol-3-yl)pyrimidin-2-yl]amino}phenyl)prop-2-enamide mesylate salt) as an Orphan Drug for the treatment of epidermal growth factor receptor mutation-positive non-small cell lung cancer.

Breakthrough Therapy Designation was granted on April 16, 2014 for the treatment of patients with metastatic, EGFR T790M mutation-positive, NSCLC, whose NSCLC has progressed during treatment with an FDA-approved, EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor.

This indication is approved under accelerated approval based on tumor response rate and duration of response. Continued approval for this indication may be contingent upon verification and description of clinical benefit in confirmatory trials.
